title: Massapequas
summary: Massapequas connects Massapequa territory with south shore shell-heap and homeland context. The map placement is approximate and avoids archaeological, burial, residential, or looting-risk locations.
address_label: Massapequa south shore territory, Nassau County, New York (approximate public area)
why_this_matters: The fortified village at Fort Neck served as a major center for the Massapequa people before becoming the site of a devastating mid-seventeenth-century battle against colonial forces. Remembering this stronghold challenges the assumption of peaceful early colonization, highlighting instead the violent displacements Native communities endured to defend their ancestral homelands.
introduction_content:
Massapequa territory extended along the south shore from Seaford toward Islip and north into the center of Long Island. Fort Neck is remembered as an important settlement and fortified place. Colonial accounts describe conflict there in the seventeenth century, but Massapequa history is larger than colonial violence and includes continuing presence, diplomacy, land agreements, and community memory.

The Massapequa people took part in many land agreements and political relationships with Dutch and English colonists. Shell heaps, village places, and remembered names throughout the area speak to long-standing Massapequa life along the south shore. Tackapousha, a Massapequa sachem, appears in many records as an important leader navigating colonial pressure and defending Native land rights.
